title: Why low training error does not guarantee better performance

paragraphs.text: The training set is used to fit parameters, and the validation set is used to choose a configuration. Use the final test set after selection is complete; repeatedly adjusting a model based on test results brings test information into the selection process.
A model may learn patterns, or it may follow noise in the sample. A better fit to the training data does not guarantee better performance on unseen data.
Model complexity, sample size, noise, and the data split all affect the results you observe. A degree that performs better in one experiment is not a rule that applies to every dataset.
This experiment shows mean squared error on specific synthetic data. Changing parameters provides observations; explanations and transfer answers provide additional evidence of understanding.

questions.text: How would you explain very low training error but poor performance on new data?
When you say performance, do you mean training data or data not used for fitting?
How could you distinguish learning a pattern from following noise?
With the sample and noise held constant, how might training and validation error change as the degree increases?
Use your observations to explain the relationship between training error and generalization again.
If you repeatedly choose the best configuration using the same test set, is that result still independent evidence of generalization? Why?
